Q5421.L2t: Muscle cells hold only a small amount of ATP and must constantly resynthesize it through phosphocreatine, glycolysis and oxidative metabolism.
Q5421.L3t: The ATP already in muscle is tiny in quantity and is used up almost immediately in all-out effort, before the phosphocreatine system, which itself lasts only around ten seconds, takes over.
Q5421.L4t: The stored ATP in muscle runs out within a couple of seconds of maximal effort.
Q5421.L2f: Muscle ATP is stored mainly in the liver and carried to working muscles by the blood during sprinting.
Q5421.L3f: Muscle keeps a large reserve of ATP that can power maximal effort for about a third of a minute before other systems are needed.
Q5421.L4f: The ATP store in muscle can fuel high-intensity exercise for roughly twenty seconds.
